NOT a defect at all. envelope is the single entry in verify-walk.mjs SERVE_STRIPPED_LEAVES: the serve deliberately strips it to null (stripZombieEnvelopeFromFacets, WDLL 3.7 anti-zombie) and the walk requires it to be EXACTLY null on the served payload. THE ANSWER. This is the only leaf in the walk's required set that the bake genuinely owns, genuinely writes, and left as a four-state violation. It is what Hays failed its 2026-09-10 staging walk on, and it is what this card closes.

theSecondQuestionAnswered.soTheGapIsSmallerThanFeared_andTheRealFi: The four-state gap turned out to be ONE leaf. Nothing else in the walk's 28 is unowned and defective. But closing it does NOT close the defect class, and the measurement says so directly: `", TX 78756"` satisfies BP-CONTENT-01 perfectly. A non-empty string is a `value` by the walk's own classifier. Of the eight named street-less parcels in the live verification run, the factory's TWO graders together (BP-CONTENT-01 plus the S1 sentinel family) catch FIVE and MISS THREE -- `", TX"` (16,010 Travis rows on that exact string), `", WACO, TX 76705"` (McLennan) and `", CEDAR CREEK, TX 78612"` (Bastrop). Across the whole population the S1 regex pair catches 124,319 of the 147,199 street-less rows, 84.5%. The four-state contract asks whether a cell has a DECLARED STATE. It does not ask whether the value means anything. Those are different questions and only the first has a control.
